messages.author: 4d7ad7ef3cf75f92
messages.subject: adding labels into bar plot
parts:
Hello.
I have next R code for producing labels for bar plot (provided by
Stuart Sharples)
It works fine for dataset "diamonds" of package "ggplot2"
BUT it does not work for any other my own dataset!
What could be the problem?

It gives next error after a line
# finally, add the labels to dplot
dplot + geom_text(data = my.labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label))


Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'X' not found

X - is some variable in my dataset (variable cut in dataset
"diamonds")

I checked - X is presented in my dataset...


#
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(ggplot2)
dplot <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(clarity, fill = cut)) +
geom_bar(position = "fill")


# cross tabulate the two variables of interest
xt <- table(diamonds$cut, diamonds$clarity)
# turn counts in to column proportions
xt <- prop.table(xt, margin = 2)
# xt is the information we want to print, however we need to
calculate
# where we want to print


# start by calculating the cumulative proportions (the tops of each of
the
bars)
cum.xt <- xt
for (m in 2:nrow(cum.xt)) {
cum.xt[m, ] <- cum.xt[m-1, ] + cum.xt[m, ]



}


# calculate the midpoints in each of the bars, these will be the
label
positions
label.positions <- xt

for (m in 2:nrow(label.positions)) {
label.positions[m, ] <- cum.xt[m-1, ] + xt[m, ] / 2



}


label.positions[1, ] <- label.positions[1,] / 2

# to keep things tidy collect all this information in to a data frame
xt <- melt(xt)
xt$value <- round(xt$value, 2)
label.positions <- melt(label.positions)


my.labels <- data.frame(x = xt$Var.2, y = label.positions$value,
label = xt$value)


# finally, add the labels to dplot
dplot + geom_text(data = my.labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label))


# but as you can see there's not enough room for the categories
# with small proportions so let's remove them
my.labels <- subset(my.labels, label > 0.025)


# add a bit of transparency to the text and change the colour to
white
# so it does not distract readers from the actual graphic
dplot + geom_text(data = my.labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
alpha = 0.6, colour = "white")

parts:
If you change the variable name to something else does it affect the error? 

Sometimes there are problems when you put data= into the original ggplot() call. Try taking everything out of ggplot() and put it into your geom_bar() call instead and see if that fixes your error.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: adding labels into bar plot
parts:
Well, you showed us the example that apparently worked, but you didn't
provide sufficient data or code to indicate what didn't work. I don't
see how anyone can help you without that information. The data don't
have to be real, just structured so that the code you run on it
triggers the error you're experiencing. Using dput(dataobject) to
present the data is preferred - copy the result you get from your
console into an e-mail and the receiver who does the converse
operation on his/her machine will see the same data you do, with the
same structure. That's often helpful in diagnosing problems and may be
very relevant in this case. Keep the test data reasonably small,
however; we don't need to see 5K observations with 500 variables in
dput() form.

Before you send it off, check the structure of your data against the
diamonds data (e.g., str(diamonds)) - a mismatch in data type between
the diamonds data and your data may be the culprit, so check that
first. If the problem still persists after checking, send your data
and non-working code back to the list.

Dennis

Hi!
Thanks, Brandon!
Now i works after putting everything from ggplot2() into geom_bar():

dplot <- ggplot() +
geom_bar(data=myDF, aes(X, fill = Y), position = "fill")
+
coord_flip()

instead of using

dplot <- ggplot(data=myDF, aes(X, fill = Y)) +
geom_bar(position = "fill") +
coord_flip()


So, there is a bug in package ggplot2 ?

Jüri.


PS.
Thanks Dennis, too.
I will use Your approach to create my postings in future...
